newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to sell first part of state bank in 97.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to sell first part of state bank in 97.

text.p: The Argentine government will sell 92 percent of state mortgage institution Banco Hipotecario and reap between $2.0 billion and $3.0 billion from the sale, bank chairman Pablo Rojo said Thursday.
Rojo told reporters that the first portion of shares, between 20 and 30 percent of the package, will be offered to the public in mid 1997.

"It will be a privatization in batches like that of (oil company) YPF so that its management independence can be maintained... There is no possibility that Hipotecario will remain in the hands of one group or bank," Rojo said.
Proceeds of the privatization will be used to create a fiduciary fund to finance public works programs in infrastructure and social projects.
The fund will begin operating before the sale thanks to a bridge loan by its underwriters who will sell the shares in local and international markets.

The government will retain five percent of the stock, which will give it veto power over board decisions. The remaining three percent will be sold to the bank's employees, who will have a right to one seat at the board.
Net assets of the bank, which returned to health after teetering near bankruptcy in 1989, are now at $2.6 billion. Net profits in 1995 were $327 million.
The bank estimates similar profits in 1996, Rojo said. In the first half of this year, profits were $150 million.
